create_chart.description: Draw a bar, horizontal bar, stacked bar, line, area, scatter, pie or donut chart from your labels and numbers, as a PNG or SVG. Returns a link to the picture, ready-made HTML and Markdown to show it in an email, page or README, the colour of each series, and the file itself when asked.
create_chart.name: create_chart

parameters.description: What kind of chart to draw. Bar, line and area charts can compare several series; pie and donut charts show one set of numbers as shares of a whole.
parameters.name: chart_type

parameters.description: The name of each point along the bottom of the chart, or of each slice of a pie, in the same order as the numbers. Leave empty to number them 1, 2, 3. A comma inside a label becomes a space.
parameters.name: labels

parameters.description: The numbers to chart, one for each label. Use this for a single set of numbers, or Series for several.
parameters.name: values

parameters.description: Several sets of numbers to compare on one bar, line, area or scatter chart: give each a name and its numbers, one for each label, such as Revenue: 12, 19, 8, 24. ChartBytes draws no legend, so the result lists each series' colour for you to show.
parameters.name: series

parameters.description: A title shown above the chart. Leave empty for none.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: PNG works everywhere, email included. SVG stays sharp at any size and is smaller, but many email apps don't show it.
parameters.name: format

parameters.description: How wide the chart is. 600 by default.
parameters.name: width

parameters.description: How tall the chart is. 300 by default.
parameters.name: height

parameters.description: Off by default, because the link is all an email, a chat message or a document needs. Turn it on when a later step needs the file itself: attaching it to an email, uploading it to storage, or posting it as a file.
parameters.display_name: Also save the chart as a file
parameters.name: save_as_file

chart_type.description: The kind of chart: bar, hbar, stacked, line, area, scatter, pie or donut.

content_type.description: The saved file's type, e.g. image/png, or '' when not saved.

document_ref.description: The saved file's document reference, or '' when not saved.

documents.description: The saved chart as a document, ready to attach to a later step. Empty when it was not saved.

content_type.description: The file's type: image/png or image/svg+xml.

filename.description: The file's name, from the chart type and its title, e.g. 'chartbytes-bar-chart-quarterly-sales.png'.

url.description: A URL that serves the stored file.

file_size_bytes.description: The saved file's size in bytes, or 0 when not saved.

file_url.description: A URL that serves the saved file, or '' when not saved.

format.description: The picture's format: png or svg.

image_tag.description: The same link as an HTML tag, with alt text and the chart's width and height, for a step that writes an email or a page.

labels.description: The label of each point or slice, in order: 1, 2, 3 when none were given.

legend.description: The colour of each series (each slice, for a pie or donut), in order, for writing a legend next to the chart: ChartBytes draws none.

color.description: Its colour as a hex code, e.g. #3B82F6.

name.description: The series' name, or the slice's label.

markdown.description: The same link as a Markdown image, for a README, Notion or a chat message.

saved_as_file.description: True when the chart was also saved as a file (Also save the chart as a file). The file fields are empty otherwise.

title.description: The chart's title, or '' when it has none.

url.description: A link to the chart's picture. It shows the chart anywhere a picture can go: an email, a chat message, a document or a web page.

description: Turn your numbers into bar, line, area, scatter, pie and donut chart images that show anywhere a picture can: emails, chat messages, documents and READMEs.
